blocks.text: The five key choices

blocks.label: C1
blocks.lead: Inherit the TUI reducer doctrine.
blocks.text: Parse only three live frame shapes (system.init, text_delta, result); everything else settles at the turn boundary via GET ?since=. internal/chat/reduce.go is a complete, charter-documented reference the epic can nearly transliterate. Interrupt is a NORMAL result outcome, never an error; the 8s interrupt wedge timer and the client-local queued badge (D12) port directly to touch.

blocks.label: C2
blocks.lead: Render settled rows from PortableDoc blocks.
blocks.text: Assistant rows carry server-computed blocks (D8); non-text rows arrive as six typed chat blocks (chat-tool-diff, chat-todo, chat-thinking, chat-approval, chat-question, chat-plan) that internal/pdrender/chat_blocks.go already decodes. Cross-lane fork: shell-and-cache floated native rendering from source_markdown - for chat tool rows, source_markdown is NOT the rich form; blocks win here and the capstone must rule the renderer question once.

blocks.label: C3
blocks.lead: Session list = one fleet SSE + rollup.
blocks.text: One life-of-process stream (GET /v1/chat/events: snapshot/state/heartbeat/title, opaque epoch:seq cursor) folds into a pure herd reducer; GET /v1/chat/rollup drives the app badge. blocks.label: C4
blocks.lead: Credential: Cloud-mediated, per-user, workspace-bound chat token.
blocks.text: The one hard piece. Recommended path B below: a new Cloud endpoint - the JSON-bearer sibling of mint_studio_link - that lets ANY team member obtain a scoped chat token for the workspace the cascade selected. blocks.text: What we learned

content.value: - and got stronger under storm scrutiny. The surprises:

blocks.label: L1
blocks.lead: The TUI doctrine is accidentally mobile-first.
blocks.text: Ephemeral live deltas + turn-boundary settlement + caller-owned cursors were designed for terminal resilience, but they are exactly the architecture an app that gets backgrounded every 30 seconds needs. Nothing about mobile requires inventing sync.

blocks.label: L2
blocks.lead: Auth is the ONLY structurally hard piece.
blocks.text: Five credential paths exist; none hands a plain member a portable scoped bearer. The studio-link path already proves Cloud-mediated JIT provision works - it just returns a cookie instead of a bearer. The epic's hard build is a JSON sibling of mint_studio_link scoped DOWN to the cascade's picked workspace instead of UP to Default-workspace owner.

blocks.label: L3
blocks.lead: Native push is 100% greenfield.
blocks.text: The corpus sweep found zero APNs/FCM anywhere. scc-w13-notify-channels (open, 0/4 criteria) is browser Web Push + webhook only. The instance-side Notifier seam (needs_you / finished_while_away, per-kind opt-out, debounce) is real and data-driven - but a native push channel is a new ask, not filed work.

blocks.label: L4
blocks.lead: The manifest hides chat from its own token.
blocks.text: Confirmed live with file:line and an intentional regression pin (capabilities.ex:167-178 + capabilities_manifest_test.exs:796-830). A least-privilege mobile client is the first consumer for whom this documented hole becomes a blocker.

blocks.label: L5
blocks.lead: Failure signals were built for operators, not products.
blocks.text: One collapsed 503 for four distinct host failures; up to 30 minutes of silence on mid-turn host loss. Fine when the operator IS the host owner in a terminal; not fine on a phone.

blocks.label: L6
blocks.lead: Chat is workspace-scoped. The cascade stops early.
blocks.text: The wish's five-level cascade (server -> workspace -> project -> dataset) lands at WORKSPACE for the chat tab - chat sessions have no project/dataset dimension. The app's chat tab should pin at the cascade's workspace level and say so in its UI model, not fake deeper scoping. Tenancy depth differs per tab across all three surfaces - a capstone ruling.

blocks.label: L7
blocks.lead: Premises that fell.
blocks.text: The /papers/barkpark-cloud-goal framing lives only in session memory - no such Paper exists in the corpus. The D1..D60h decision space is actually THREE numbering series sharing low numbers (chat charter, wsc session-card charter, herd h-series). And the wire-contract prose in the chat charter still reads require_admin - the live pipeline is require_chat_access; quote the code, not the charter.

content.value: - and got stronger under storm scrutiny. The surprises:

blocks.label: L1
blocks.lead: The TUI doctrine is accidentally mobile-first.
blocks.text: Ephemeral live deltas + turn-boundary settlement + caller-owned cursors were designed for terminal resilience, but they are exactly the architecture an app that gets backgrounded every 30 seconds needs. Nothing about mobile requires inventing sync.

blocks.label: L2
blocks.lead: Auth is the ONLY structurally hard piece.
blocks.text: Five credential paths exist; none hands a plain member a portable scoped bearer. The studio-link path already proves Cloud-mediated JIT provision works - it just returns a cookie instead of a bearer. The epic's hard build is a JSON sibling of mint_studio_link scoped DOWN to the cascade's picked workspace instead of UP to Default-workspace owner.

blocks.label: L3
blocks.lead: Native push is 100% greenfield.
blocks.text: The corpus sweep found zero APNs/FCM anywhere. scc-w13-notify-channels (open, 0/4 criteria) is browser Web Push + webhook only. The instance-side Notifier seam (needs_you / finished_while_away, per-kind opt-out, debounce) is real and data-driven - but a native push channel is a new ask, not filed work.

blocks.label: L4
blocks.lead: The manifest hides chat from its own token.
blocks.text: Confirmed live with file:line and an intentional regression pin (capabilities.ex:167-178 + capabilities_manifest_test.exs:796-830). A least-privilege mobile client is the first consumer for whom this documented hole becomes a blocker.

blocks.label: L5
blocks.lead: Failure signals were built for operators, not products.
blocks.text: One collapsed 503 for four distinct host failures; up to 30 minutes of silence on mid-turn host loss. Fine when the operator IS the host owner in a terminal; not fine on a phone.

blocks.label: L6
blocks.lead: Chat is workspace-scoped. The cascade stops early.
blocks.text: The wish's five-level cascade (server -> workspace -> project -> dataset) lands at WORKSPACE for the chat tab - chat sessions have no project/dataset dimension. The app's chat tab should pin at the cascade's workspace level and say so in its UI model, not fake deeper scoping. Tenancy depth differs per tab across all three surfaces - a capstone ruling.

blocks.lead: Premises that fell.
blocks.text: The /papers/barkpark-cloud-goal framing lives only in session memory - no such Paper exists in the corpus. The D1..D60h decision space is actually THREE numbering series sharing low numbers (chat charter, wsc session-card charter, herd h-series). And the wire-contract prose in the chat charter still reads require_admin - the live pipeline is require_chat_access; quote the code, not the charter.

BARKPARK TASKS MOBILE / PREPARATION STACK / LANE: CHAT AS THE THIRD SIBLING CLIENT

Mobile Chat, the Third Sibling Client

The interview pinned mobile chat precisely: the existing Barkpark chat-sessions surface (Claude sessions) brought to the phone as a third sibling client beside the bp chat TUI and the Studio GUI. This Paper is the definitive contract map for that client. The verdict up front: the entire core loop - list, create, send, stream, interrupt, approve, resume - can be written against the frozen /v1/chat wire contract with zero new Elixir. The engine is already multi-client by proof. The one structurally hard piece is the credential a phone should hold; everything else on the epic-adds list is small and server-side. Crown paper: barkpark-tasks-mobile-capstone.

Status: preparation, nothing built. Every fact below is pinned to origin/main file:line or to a live probe of guerrilla (both GET /v1/chat/sessions and GET /v1/chat/rollup returned 200 on 2026-07-23 - origin/main IS the deployed truth). Sibling lane papers: identity-cascade, product-shapes, shell-and-cache, tasks-papers-reading; the capstone combines all five.
§

What we will create

A mobile chat surface that inherits the TUI's doctrine wholesale, because that doctrine is accidentally a perfect mobile-backgrounding architecture: minimal live parse, settle everything at the turn boundary. Live SSE deltas are ephemeral by design; settled truth is Postgres rows with monotonic seq. Backgrounding the app IS the already-proven reconnect path - on foreground, GET /sessions/:id?since=maxSeq then re-attach SSE with Last-Event-ID=maxSeq. No sync engine, no local write queue, no conflict resolution: the server owns truth, the phone owns a cursor.

10
client routes live today
6
typed chat blocks, server-synthesized
0
new Elixir for the core loop
38
sessions live on guerrilla

The five key choices

C1
Inherit the TUI reducer doctrine. Parse only three live frame shapes (system.init, text_delta, result); everything else settles at the turn boundary via GET ?since=. internal/chat/reduce.go is a complete, charter-documented reference the epic can nearly transliterate. Interrupt is a NORMAL result outcome, never an error; the 8s interrupt wedge timer and the client-local queued badge (D12) port directly to touch.
C2
Render settled rows from PortableDoc blocks. Assistant rows carry server-computed blocks (D8); non-text rows arrive as six typed chat blocks (chat-tool-diff, chat-todo, chat-thinking, chat-approval, chat-question, chat-plan) that internal/pdrender/chat_blocks.go already decodes. One renderer serves chat transcripts AND the papers tab. Cross-lane fork: shell-and-cache floated native rendering from source_markdown - for chat tool rows, source_markdown is NOT the rich form; blocks win here and the capstone must rule the renderer question once.
C3
Session list = one fleet SSE + rollup. One life-of-process stream (GET /v1/chat/events: snapshot/state/heartbeat/title, opaque epoch:seq cursor) folds into a pure herd reducer; GET /v1/chat/rollup drives the app badge. Port herd.go's fold and ranking - but add the title-frame case herd.go itself is missing (gap found this run).
C4
Credential: Cloud-mediated, per-user, workspace-bound chat token. The one hard piece. Recommended path B below: a new Cloud endpoint - the JSON-bearer sibling of mint_studio_link - that lets ANY team member obtain a scoped chat token for the workspace the cascade selected. Requires fixing the D36 capabilities hole so a chat token can discover its own noun. Couples to the identity-cascade lane's ruling.
C5
Push notifications ride Cloud, not the instance. For a Cloud-exclusive v1 app, a single Cloud-held APNs/FCM identity relaying off the instance's chat_blocked webhook / Notifier channel beats teaching every self-hosted instance to hold push certs. This is the app's only genuinely new distributed system - and it is native-push greenfield: scc-w13-notify-channels only ever gets you browser Web Push.

The credential question - rivals, honestly

OptionWhat the phone holdsVerdict
A. Instance admin token (Cloud already stores it: Registry.reveal_admin_token):global chat scope + full instance adminReject for GA. Works day one, but a pocket device holding root on every workspace is the wrong trust posture. Acceptable at most as a dev-mode shortcut.
B. Per-user workspace chat token, minted via a new Cloud-mediated seamchat-only bearer bound to ONE workspace (Auth.create_chat_token/3, the D48 single literal)Recommended. Least privilege, tenancy-clean, reuses the shipped ChatTokenController + the proven studio-link JIT-provision pattern. Costs: new Cloud endpoint, the D36 manifest fix, and the phone likely holds a second token for tasks/papers - see the cross-lane contradiction below.
C. New user-principal chat scope (airdrop user-principal seam)one identity, per-user authorizationCleanest long-term, biggest build. Defensible as the v2 destination; too much for the founding wave.
Cross-lane contradiction, not papered over: identity-cascade proposes one app token carrying [read, write, chat]; tasks-papers-reading proved paper block-ops require ingest-secret or admin. Whatever token strategy wins, the eventual paper-editing ambition silently contradicts a least-privilege chat token unless the epic declares a per-user ops-route seam. The capstone must rule this once, for all three tabs.

How rich is chat EXCELLENTLY?

Studio's ChatLive is 6,756 lines of render vocabulary; the TUI proves a far smaller set already feels excellent in a constrained medium. Recommendation: TUI-grade live tail + full six-block settled richness, plus three mobile-worthy upgrades the TUI lacks: a context/headroom indicator (derived client-side from persisted last_context_tokens/context_window - no server work), the compaction notice, and answerable question cards IF the /answer route ships (see epic-adds). The nine LiveView-only surfaces are enumerated below with a reproduce/proxy/scope-out ruling each. The user rules the final bar - it fixes the client's parser budget.

§

How the system works today

The /v1/chat contract, endpoint by endpoint

All client routes ride [:api, :require_chat_access] (the chat-tui charter's require_admin prose is stale - Connectors D18 replaced it). Scope resolution (require_chat_access.ex): token with admin permission resolves :global; workspace-bound token with chat permission resolves {:workspace, ws}; chat token with NULL workspace is 403 fail-closed. Wrong-tenant session ids 404 (indistinguishable from missing, Connectors D19a) - and the SSE route scopes get_session BEFORE subscribing, so a foreign tenant cannot join a live stream by guessing a UUID.

RouteRequestResponse / notes
GET /v1/chat/sessions?archived=-{sessions:[...]} sidebar shape, cap 50, no pagination; rows carry agent_state/agent_state_at (D50h) for the herd cold-mount
POST /v1/chat/sessions{provider?, execution_target?, execution_host_id?, mode?, model?, effort?}201 full session. Id server-minted, cwd server-owned, bypassPermissions unrepresentable. NO runtime spawns here - an offline host still 201s; failure surfaces on first send
GET /v1/chat/sessions/:id?since=seq-Full continuity struct (draft, mode, model_choice, effort_choice, title, rail_snapshot, token/cost metrics) + messages seq-asc; assistant rows carry PortableDoc blocks beside source_markdown (D8). ?since= returns only newer rows - the turn-boundary tail refetch
PATCH /v1/chat/sessions/:id{draft? | mode? | model_choice? | effort_choice? | title?}Strict allowlist - unknown key 400; archived sessions reject writes. This is the D14 continuity write, fired on leave/switch
POST .../:id/messages{content <= 64KiB}202 {accepted:true}. Server does not distinguish fresh turn from mid-turn steer (D12) - the queued badge is client-local. Runtime failures: 503 chat_unavailable (see failure matrix)
POST .../:id/interrupt-202 {request_id|null}; no-op when idle. Ack is semantically EMPTY - truth is the terminal result frame (aborted_streaming), a NORMAL outcome
POST .../:id/approval{request_id, decision: allow|deny}204, idempotent; deny injects the fixed 'Denied by operator.' D22 forbids caller-supplied updatedInput
GET .../:id/eventsSSEPer-session stream, grammar below. Viewers never own runtimes (D24) - history stays readable when nothing can execute
GET /v1/chat/eventsSSEFleet stream: snapshot/state/heartbeat/title, opaque epoch:seq Last-Event-ID, 256-flip ring, degrade-to-snapshot
GET /v1/chat/rollup-{counts:{blocked,working,idle,unknown}, precedence} - precedence blocked>working>idle>unknown, byte-matched to Go herdRank (D64h)
POST /w/:ws/p/:proj/v1/chat/tokens{label, dataset}Owner/admin-only mint; permissions HARDCODED [chat] in Auth.create_chat_token/3 (D36/D48); plaintext returned once. Body permissions ignored
POST /v1/chat/sessions/:id/state(host credential)Registered-host pipeline only - the phone never calls this

Wire bounds: title/request_id max 256 UTF-8 bytes; content/draft max 64 KiB; since is a non-negative int64. Over-limit means canonical 400 before any store/runtime call.

SSE grammar - both streams

# Per-session stream: GET /v1/chat/sessions/:id/events
replay (rows seq > Last-Event-ID):
  id: <seq>
  event: message        data: <persisted message row JSON>
live (no id, unreplayable by design - D5):
  event: chat            data: raw claude stream-json frame, verbatim
  event: runtime         data: codex runtime frames
  event: permission      data: approval ask {request_id, ...}
  event: workflow        data: compact workflow summary
  event: exit            data: {"status": int|null,
                               "reason": "clean|failed_start|crashed|idle_reaped|unknown"}
: keepalive every 30s. Never shed-and-close (D5/D24). Stderr structurally cannot leak (D23).

# Fleet stream: GET /v1/chat/events   (cursor = opaque "<epoch>:<seq>")
  event: snapshot   id: e:s   data: {"sessions":[{session_id, agent_state, ts, title}]}
  event: state      id: e:s   data: {session_id, agent_state, ts, title: null}
  event: heartbeat  (no id)   data: {session_id, ts}
  event: title      (no id)   data: {session_id, title}          # D69h, on origin/main
ring holds 256 state FLIPS only; wrong epoch or out-of-ring cursor -> fresh scoped snapshot
agent_state enum: working|blocked|idle|unknown; heartbeat 60s; stall sweep 150s (every 5min);
BlockedSweeper 60s keys on pending ask ROWS, never agent_state

Auth today - and what a phone cannot obtain

The credential-flow probe mapped every path from Cloud identity to data-plane credential. The gap is sharp: no endpoint anywhere hands a plain team member a portable, scoped bearer token. The CLI's cloud-connect path is team-admin-gated server-side (cloud router.ex:1848 require_team_admin) and the CLI itself bails for members (setup_cloud_login.go:179). Studio-link IS member-reachable - but its ticket consume sets a browser session cookie, never a JSON bearer (session_controller.ex ticket/2), and it grants owner-on-Default-workspace, not the cascade's selection. The bootstrap reveal is admin-gated and frozen at provision time. The chat-token mint (the right SHAPE) requires owner/admin role on the instance workspace - which nothing hands a plain member.

PathToken kindMember-reachable?
bp login device flow (RFC-8628, shipped, bp-login-ux charter)Cloud CONTROL token - by charter D3 never rides the data planeyes
GET /v1/barkparks/:id/credentialsinstance ADMIN token (root, un-scoped)team-admin only (403 for member)
POST /v1/barkparks/:id/studio-link60s single-use ticket -> browser session COOKIE; JIT-provisions user as Default-workspace owneryes - but no portable bearer
GET /v1/barkparks/:id/bootstrapread-only token frozen to one {ws, project, dataset} at provisionadmin only
POST /w/:ws/p/:proj/v1/chat/tokenschat-only workspace bearer - the right shape for the phonerequires instance owner/admin role
The D36 manifest hole (confirmed live, pinned): a workspace chat-only token is AUTHORIZED for /v1/chat at runtime, yet projects capabilities tier none - tier_for_token/1 (capabilities.ex:167-178) only recognizes admin/write/read, and all 7 chat core_cmds are tier admin, so the chat noun is existence-hidden from its own token. Pinned as intentional at capabilities_manifest_test.exs:796-830. The minting endpoint that produces exactly this token shape shipped in PR #3174. For a manifest-driven mobile client this stops being an edge case and becomes a day-one discoverability blocker - the fix (remap chat into tier_for_token) is a named epic-add, charter-gated on the hot connectors surface.

Registered-host execution: the failure matrix

Sessions execute managed (subprocess on the API server) or registered_host (enrolled laptop via fenced lease dispatch: enrollment TTL 600s, credential 30d, lease 60s, online window 90s). The scoping verdict is GOOD news: a workspace-bound chat token can create sessions on its own workspace's already-enrolled hosts - create-time validation only checks UUID shape (chat_controller.ex:860-885), owner_workspace_id is stamped from the caller's own scope (never client-controlled), and host resolution is confined to that workspace (context.ex:181-198; foreign host ids fail closed as host_not_found). Only ENROLLING a new host is owner-gated. The failure signals, however, are hostile to a first-party client:

ScenarioWhat the phone seesAnchor
Host offline at session create201 Created - create never touches the host; no runtime spawns until first sendchat_controller.ex create/2 ~L107-131
First send: host offline / never registered / provider missingOne undifferentiated 503 {"error":"chat_unavailable"} - the specific reason (host_offline vs host_not_found vs provider_not_ready) is logged server-side onlychat_controller.ex ensure_and_send ~L249-253
Host silently lost mid-turn (crash, network death)Silence. No lease-expiry sweeper emits an exit frame; the SSE stream just stops until the 30-minute frame-silence idle reaper fires event:exit reason=idle_reapedrecorder.ex:29 @idle_after_ms, ~L710
Host gone at resumeIdentical 503 to the create case - wire-indistinguishableruntime.ex:341-374
V1
Mobile consequence. The client needs its own turn timeout (30-60s of frame silence -> honest 'agent unreachable' UI), and the epic should file the small server fix splitting the 503 into distinct reason codes. Live reality check: all 38 guerrilla sessions are provider=claude, execution_target=managed - codex and registered_host are modeled but unexercised in production, so v1 can treat them as render-tolerated, not feature-complete.

Render vocabulary - what is free, what is LiveView-only

The transcript-content spine is genuinely dual-surface: prose rows, the six typed chat blocks, agents rail (persisted rail_snapshot, D47), workflow strips/summaries, epic-goal lines, mode/model/effort facts, and cost metrics all decode from persisted rows + session fields that Elixir and Go already both render. A mobile client re-deriving from settled rows gets that spine near-free. Nine surfaces are LiveView-only today and never reach any client over the transport:

LiveView-only surfacev1 ruling (recommend)
MCP entity/search chips (task/paper deep-link pills, ChatToolRenderer.chip/2 - no PortableDoc block exists)Scope out v1; candidate epic-add: materialize a chip block (benefits TUI too)
Live thinking pulse (growing ~N tokens estimate)Proxy: static thinking shimmer; the settled chat-thinking block lands at boundary
Compaction notice (compact_boundary, explicitly not persisted)Reproduce cheaply from the live frame; low cost, high honesty
Context/headroom ring + cost stripReproduce client-side from persisted last_context_tokens / context_window / cost - no server work

Bypass-arm ceremony (type-to-arm danger panel)Scope out: bypassPermissions is unrepresentable over the transport anyway
Doing strip + ready-task picker (hand-task claims)Scope out v1 chat tab; the TASKS tab is the app's native home for this
Needs-you strip 5-state granularity (approve>answer>plan-ready>running>done)Accept the TUI's coarser 4-state herd rank for v1 (blocked/working/stalled/idle)

Client reducer gap to carry forward: origin/main's herd.go folds snapshot/state/heartbeat but has no case for the title frame - event:title falls through and is dropped, so titles go stale on an open list. The server side of D69h shipped (#5561) with Elixir-only tests. The mobile reducer must add the title case (nil keeps held title, mirroring state semantics) rather than porting herd.go 1:1 - and fixing herd.go itself is a friendly co-benefit epic-add.

§

What we learned

The premise held completely - and got stronger under storm scrutiny. The surprises:

L1
The TUI doctrine is accidentally mobile-first. Ephemeral live deltas + turn-boundary settlement + caller-owned cursors were designed for terminal resilience, but they are exactly the architecture an app that gets backgrounded every 30 seconds needs. Nothing about mobile requires inventing sync.
L2
Auth is the ONLY structurally hard piece. Five credential paths exist; none hands a plain member a portable scoped bearer. The studio-link path already proves Cloud-mediated JIT provision works - it just returns a cookie instead of a bearer. The epic's hard build is a JSON sibling of mint_studio_link scoped DOWN to the cascade's picked workspace instead of UP to Default-workspace owner.
L3
Native push is 100% greenfield. The corpus sweep found zero APNs/FCM anywhere. scc-w13-notify-channels (open, 0/4 criteria) is browser Web Push + webhook only. The instance-side Notifier seam (needs_you / finished_while_away, per-kind opt-out, debounce) is real and data-driven - but a native push channel is a new ask, not filed work.
L4
The manifest hides chat from its own token. Confirmed live with file:line and an intentional regression pin (capabilities.ex:167-178 + capabilities_manifest_test.exs:796-830). A least-privilege mobile client is the first consumer for whom this documented hole becomes a blocker.
L5
Failure signals were built for operators, not products. One collapsed 503 for four distinct host failures; up to 30 minutes of silence on mid-turn host loss. Fine when the operator IS the host owner in a terminal; not fine on a phone.
L6
Chat is workspace-scoped. The cascade stops early. The wish's five-level cascade (server -> workspace -> project -> dataset) lands at WORKSPACE for the chat tab - chat sessions have no project/dataset dimension. The app's chat tab should pin at the cascade's workspace level and say so in its UI model, not fake deeper scoping. Tenancy depth differs per tab across all three surfaces - a capstone ruling.
L7
Premises that fell. The /papers/barkpark-cloud-goal framing lives only in session memory - no such Paper exists in the corpus. The D1..D60h decision space is actually THREE numbering series sharing low numbers (chat charter, wsc session-card charter, herd h-series). And the wire-contract prose in the chat charter still reads require_admin - the live pipeline is require_chat_access; quote the code, not the charter.
